name: WSOS Baccalaureate Scholarship
value: Up to $2,500 annually before major and credit verification; then $5,000, $7,500 and $5,000 in the first, second and third years after approval. Awards are limited by remaining cost of attendance.
deadline: Application opens January 13, 2027; application and FAFSA/WASFA due February 25, 2027 (application at 9 p.m. PST); notification April 21, 2027; acceptance due May 6, 2027 at 9 p.m. PST.
apply: Complete the WSOS application with 150–500-word essays and required unofficial transcript or GED documentation; file FAFSA or WASFA and apply for federal education tax credits if eligible. No references are required. Selected students must accept and complete online orientation.
eligibility: Washington residents, including undocumented applicants, with a Washington high school credential earned by June of the application year; no prior bachelor’s degree. Requires cumulative 2.75 GPA on a 4.0 scale or a passing GED score, income at or below 125% of Washington median family income, an approved major and Washington institution, and at least three credits each fall, winter and spring. Applicants with more than 90 quarter or 60 semester credits earned after high school are ineligible; dual-enrollment credits are excluded from this entry limit.
notes: Annual renewal requires the portal form and processed FAFSA/WASFA. Maintain the college’s satisfactory academic progress. Major and credit verification requires admission to an eligible major and 90 quarter or 60 semester credits by the individual portal deadline. Maximum funding is 18 quarters or 12 semesters, reduced by prior Washington College Grant terms; application grade limits time at the initial award rate. Twelve credits qualify for the full rate; three to eleven credits receive prorated funding. Other aid can reduce or eliminate the award.

name: Golden LEAF Colleges and Universities Scholarship
value: First-year students: $3,500 annually for up to four years ($14,000 total); community college transfers: $3,500 annually for up to three years ($10,500 total).
deadline: 2027-28 cycle: applications open January 2027; application, transcript and FAFSA due March 1, 2027; awards announced May 2027
apply: Apply through the NCSEAA student portal linked by CFNC; complete North Carolina residency determination, upload a transcript with the most recent fall grades, and submit the FAFSA for the appropriate academic year.
eligibility: Graduating North Carolina high school seniors (or NC community college transfers) who are NC residents for tuition purposes, live in a qualifying rural, economically distressed NC county, have at least a 2.5 cumulative GPA and a Student Aid Index of $15,000 or less, and plan to attend a participating NC college or university full-time.
notes: Renew annually through the Golden LEAF Renewal Profile and processed FAFSA; continued financial need, at least 12 credits each semester at an approved institution, and institutional satisfactory academic progress are required. Prior college or university attendance outside dual enrollment is excluded by the CFNC rules, while current NC community college transfers are expressly eligible. The sponsor currently links a 2026–27 qualifying-county list; the 2027–28 county list is not yet confirmed.

provider: Texas FFA Association and Texas FFA Foundation
name: Texas FFA Scholarship Program
value: Individual scholarship amounts, payment schedules and continuing conditions vary by donor award; no single per-student amount applies to the whole program.
deadline: Opens January 1, 2027. Area deadlines in 2027: Areas 1 and 3, April 1 at 11:59 PM; Area 5, April 1 at 5 PM; Areas 2 and 4, April 5 at 5 PM; Area 7, April 5 at 11:59 PM; Area 12, April 8 at 11:59 PM; Area 9, April 11 at noon; Areas 8 and 10, April 12 at 11:59 PM; Area 6, April 14 according to the official events calendar, though the scholarship page still says TBD; Area 11, April 19 at 11:59 PM. Area 6's time and other time zones are unstated. State interviews June 4, 2027.
apply: Apply through the Texas FFA roster account and local area process. Upload requested signatures/documents, signed official transcript for the first 3.5 high-school years, official SAT/ACT scores and FAFSA Submission Summary/SAI. Finalists interview in official FFA dress; recipients must attend the state convention sponsor banquet and awards presentation unless an exception is approved.
eligibility: U.S. citizens who are current-year graduating seniors, active Texas FFA members this year and at least two of the previous three years, on the state roster and in good standing. Requires at least three academic years and five separate semesters of AFNR instruction in grades 9–12, SAT 1000 or ACT 19 without superscoring, top half of the class, and receipt or successful application for the current Lone Star Degree. Must intend to attend a Texas college or university that fall. Some donors require higher class rank or an approved major. Terry Foundation recipients are ineligible.
notes: More than 140 scholarships and approximately $2.4 million are aggregate annual program totals, not individual award amounts. Awards are ranked using academics, FFA experience, financial need and interviews; candidates cannot select a donor scholarship. The 2027 page requests the 2026–27 FAFSA, which may conflict with the entering college year. Confirm the required FAFSA year. Individual donor terms vary.

name: Texas 4-H Foundation Scholarships (Baccalaureate, Technical, Courageous Heart)
value: 2027 guidelines: individual awards range from $1,000 to $30,000; Courageous Heart awards are $5,000. Duration and payment schedule vary by donor.
deadline: Opens November 1, 2026; application due February 15, 2027 at 11:59 PM, time zone unstated. Mandatory interviews April 23–25, 2027 in College Station; May 2027 notifications and June 9–10, 2027 banquets appear on the current webpage. The separately located 2027 guidelines give a January 31 FAFSA completion date but conflict on the aid year and banquet year.
apply: Apply to one category in the scholarship portal. Submit experience and personal/career/financial-need narratives, supplemental records, signed county extension agent verification and school-official third-party verification before submission. Courageous Heart also requires an obstacle narrative, documentation and three support letters. Interview and donor-banquet attendance are required.
eligibility: Texas residents and U.S. citizens graduating from a Texas public, private or home high school in 2026–27; enrolled Texas 4-H members this year and at least two of the prior three years, in good standing. Apply to a Texas accredited college/university/technical school for fall 2027 and be accepted by the interview. Baccalaureate supports a bachelor’s degree; Technical supports certification with no plan to continue to a bachelor’s degree; Courageous Heart requires documented major medical, family or educational obstacles and continued 4-H/school participation. Terry Foundation recipients are excluded. Donors may impose class-rank, GPA, major or show-participation restrictions.
notes: Foundation-administered scholarships generally require passing 12 fall/spring credits, cumulative 2.0 GPA and semester reporting with transcript, schedule and donor progress letter. Summer/interim terms are not funded. Donor-administered awards can have separate terms. The public webpage still links a 2026 guidelines PDF even though it advertises 2027 events; separately located 2027 documents conflict internally on FAFSA year and banquet year. Confirm the governing 2027 application rules.

provider: Georgia Foundation for Agriculture (Georgia Farm Bureau)
name: Scholarship for Agriculture (high school seniors)
value: 2026 cycle: ten $3,000 awards; the two highest-ranked applicants were eligible for an extra $1,500. The 2027 award terms are not yet published.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; applications reopen in November for the 2027 cycle. The 2026 deadline was March 1, 2026.
apply: Use the sponsor-linked RegFox application when the 2027 form opens. The prior form is closed, and the 2027 supporting-document requirements are not yet available.
eligibility: Published 2026–27 rules: Georgia residents finishing high school in the application year, active in high-school leadership, pursuing agriculture, environmental sciences, family and consumer sciences or a related field at a University System of Georgia institution, Berry College, Emmanuel College or another accredited Georgia institution with an agriculture program. The 2027 rules have not yet been confirmed.
notes: The 2026 award was applied to spring tuition after earning at least a 3.0 GPA in the first college semester, rather than a published high-school GPA floor. The linked institution/major sample document contains older institution names and is not a confirmed 2027 list.

provider: Iowa Economic Development Authority, Iowa Arts Council
name: Iowa Scholarship for the Arts
value: 2026–27 cycle: $5,000 toward tuition, paid directly to the Iowa institution after enrollment confirmation. The 2027–28 award has not yet been published.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 deadline was April 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM, with finalist interviews on or about April 23, 2026.
apply: Prior 2026 guidelines required a SlideRoom application, artistic-vision/career essay, one teacher or equivalent professional recommendation, and three to five work samples in the intended field. Top applicants had a mandatory 15-minute interview. The full 2027 application is not yet available.
eligibility: Prior 2026 rules required Iowa residency, graduation from an Iowa high school in 2025–26, demonstrated artistic ability, and acceptance as a full-time undergraduate at an accredited Iowa institution in music, dance, visual arts, theatre, folklife or literature. Immediate family/dependents of specified agency/arts-council board members or staff were excluded. The 2027 rules have not yet been published.
notes: The prior guidelines limit reviewed written samples to five pages and audio/video to three minutes, with discipline-specific format rules. The September 16, 2026 rulemaking notice proposes updated program rules; it is a proposal, not a confirmed 2027 application cycle or adopted eligibility rule.

name: Florida Realtors Education Foundation Student Scholarship Program
value: Awards generally start at $1,000, with amounts and award counts decided annually. One award per 12 months, maximum two awards; a new application is required each year.
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; the 2026 application period is closed. Review is usually completed by the end of April.
apply: Online application with three references, including two school teachers/administrators on school letterhead. The prior 2026 application additionally required three years of academic transcripts, college acceptance letter(s), and a school ID for enrolled students. The 2027 form and full document rules are not yet posted.
eligibility: Florida residents (proof of legal Florida residency required) who are high school seniors attending an undergraduate college, or current undergraduate or graduate students. Out-of-state colleges allowed if the applicant intends to return to work in Florida. Any major; Realtors and their families may apply.
notes: Selection considers academics, financial need, leadership, Realtor-family relationship and community/family/school contributions; real-estate-related fields receive priority but any major can qualify. Current FAQ calls for three reference letters, including two from teachers or administrators on school letterhead, and an online application. Funds go to the college; claim dates are set annually, usually mid-to-late July. No automatic renewal; reapply subject to the two-award lifetime limit. The 2027 form may request additional documents.

provider: Journalism Education Foundation of New England (New England Newspaper and Press Association)
name: New England Journalism Scholarship Program
value: 2026 cycle: up to $2,000 per award for up to ten recipients. The 2027 amounts and continuing-award terms are not published.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; scholarship applications are closed for 2026.
apply: Prior cycle: submit the application form, then email PDF or Word attachments containing a cover letter, transcript, resume or biography, one recommendation, and at least three journalism pieces. Online-work links must be collected into one attachment, rather than pasted into the email.
eligibility: Prior 2026 rules: residents of Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island or Vermont who are high-school seniors or undergraduates studying journalism or a related field for fall 2026, with GPA at least 3.0. Graduate students were excluded; college location could be outside New England. The 2027 criteria are not yet confirmed.
notes: The program includes the annual MacGregor Fiske Award. Scholarship applications are currently closed for 2026; no 2027 form, deadline or renewal terms are published.

provider: Ohio News Media Foundation (Ohio News Media Association)
name: Ohio High School Journalism Scholarship
value: 2026–27 cycle: $1,000 award. The 2027–28 amount and continuing-award terms are not yet published.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 deadline was Monday, May 25, 2026.
apply: Prior 2026 application: signed PDF form, official high-school transcript, 500–750-word autobiography and one recommendation; submit by mail to the Ohio News Media Foundation or as PDF email attachments to its program contact.
eligibility: Prior 2026–27 rules: graduating seniors at Ohio high schools with at least a 2.5 GPA, intending to study journalism, advertising, marketing, communications or another newspaper-industry-related field at an accredited college or university. The 2027–28 rules are unconfirmed.
notes: The 2026 PDF required all material to arrive by end of business on May 25, 2026, without an exact time or time zone. No 2027 deadline appears in the current official page or linked application; third-party projected dates are not official confirmation.

name: NYFB Agricultural Youth Scholarship
value: Published awards: $250 for each district winner; state first place $3,000 and second place $2,000. No 2027-specific award or renewal terms are published.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet announced; applications for 2026 scholarships have closed.
apply: Apply through the New York Farm Bureau scholarship process when the next form is released. District winners advance to state selection. The 2027 application materials and submission method are not yet published.
eligibility: Published requirements: graduating high-school senior pursuing an agricultural career through college or skilled-trades training, living or working on a farm or actively involved in agriculture, with NYFB Family or Student membership. Students can join free; applicants under 18 need a parent/guardian signature. The page does not specify a separate New York residency or New York high-school attendance requirement.
notes: Applications for 2026 are closed and the sponsor explicitly says to watch for 2027 updates. No GPA or specific agriculture-major requirement is stated; skilled-trades pathways can qualify.

name: Michael P. Voiles Memorial Scholarship for Insurance and Agriculture
value: $1,500 per recipient, paid to the institution; two recipients annually. May renew for up to three additional years at the Foundation’s discretion.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 application period closed on March 31, 2026.
apply: Complete the sponsor form with a resume and recommendation from a teacher, counselor, professor, community leader or school administrator. High-school applicants provide a transcript and four-year degree-program acceptance notice; college applicants provide a college transcript.
eligibility: Missouri residents who hold current Missouri Farm Bureau membership themselves or through a parent, grandparent or guardian; high-school seniors entering a four-year institution or current four-year undergraduates, enrolled that fall in an insurance or agriculture-related field. Eligible examples include business administration, finance-insurance and mathematics with actuarial science.
notes: Renewal requires a 3.0 GPA, continued undergraduate insurance/agriculture study and at least 12 credits each semester; award and renewal decisions are discretionary. The directory’s $3,000 is the annual program total, while the specific program page states a $1,500 stipend for each of two students. The 2027 application dates are not yet published.

name: INFB Ag Impact Scholarships
value: The current program description lists three $2,000 awards. Future-cycle award duration and renewal terms are not published.
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; check back in January 2027. The 2026 deadline was March 1.
apply: Use the Indiana Farm Bureau scholarship portal when the next form opens. One application is considered for eligible state and most county/district awards; some county forms are separate. The 2027 Ag Impact application materials are not yet published.
eligibility: The current program description covers graduating high-school seniors pursuing agricultural careers with substantial 4-H and/or FFA involvement and leadership. The February 2026 announcement additionally required the applicant or immediate family to have three consecutive years of Indiana Farm Bureau membership; that condition has not yet been confirmed for 2027.
notes: The sponsor says to check back in January 2027; it has not announced a 2027 deadline. The 2026 announcement allowed tuition, housing, books and other educational expenses. An agricultural career is required, but the current description does not specify one mandatory major or GPA floor.

name: Linda and Wayne Zaunbrecher Scholarship
value: 2026–27 cycle: up to $3,000 per recipient, up to five winners; reapply for up to four consecutive years total, with amounts varying annually. The 2027–28 award is unconfirmed.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the page covers 2026 awards (made in May 2026) and lists no specific deadline date.
apply: Apply through one parish Farm Bureau; each parish may submit one candidate for statewide selection. The linked Jotform application is closed, and the 2027 materials and parish deadlines are not published.
eligibility: Prior 2026 rules required spring 2026 high-school graduation, applicant or parent Louisiana Farm Bureau membership, cumulative 2.5 GPA over four high-school years, agricultural studies at an accredited Louisiana institution starting the next fall and continuing in spring. The next-cycle rules are not yet published.
notes: Prior rules required 2.5 GPA after the first fall term and for each later full-time term, continued agriculture major and annual membership, with renewal applications each term. No deferral or summer funding. Early graduation ended payments unless immediately followed by agricultural graduate study. Selection included academic record, ACT scores, leadership, Farm Bureau activities and financial need.

name: Next Generation Hoosier Educators Scholarship
value: Up to $10,000 each year for four academic years (renewable)
deadline: 2027–28 applications open October 15, 2026 and close January 31, 2027; decisions by email in April 2027. The current webpage does not state a deadline time or time zone.
apply: Apply through a full student ScholarTrack account and file the FAFSA annually. The currently linked FAQ asks for high-school academic, extracurricular and employment information plus a writing response of up to 250 words; the exact prompt appears in the application. Selected students must complete award instructions and a promissory note.
eligibility: Indiana residents who are U.S. citizens or eligible noncitizens, current high-school seniors or Indiana college students, and graduates of an accredited Indiana high school or non-accredited non-public Indiana high school. Requires at least two full academic years of remaining scholarship use and either top-20% high-school class rank, top-20% ACT/SAT performance, or high-school cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Must study full-time in an eligible Indiana educator-preparation program leading to Indiana teaching licensure. Graduate students and already licensed teachers are excluded; no federal grant/loan overpayment or default.
notes: Renew with a 3.0 college GPA, 30 annual credits or equivalent, annual FAFSA and ScholarTrack renewal form. Funding is limited by cost of attendance and other gift aid, with up to $40,000 total over four years. Requires five years of full-time teaching at an eligible Indiana K–12 public, charter or nonpublic school after graduation. Failure to complete the program or service converts the prorated amount used to a loan with interest; the currently linked FAQ states 7% fixed interest. Eligible noncitizens include specified refugee/asylee/parole categories; student/exchange visas and DACA are excluded.

provider: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development
name: A+ Scholarship Program
value: Unpaid tuition and general fees after federal non-loan aid, subject to funding and an annual per-hour cap; 2026-27 cap $240 per credit or $8 per clock hour. The 2027-28 cap is not published.
deadline: No separate statewide scholarship application deadline; complete the FAFSA annually and confirm the participating institution’s processing deadlines.
apply: Enter a written A+ agreement before high school graduation, complete the school’s A+ requirements, and provide the A+ transcript certification to a participating institution. Make a good-faith annual FAFSA effort; a Federal Student Aid Estimator applies at schools not participating in federal Title IV aid.
eligibility: U.S. citizens or permanent residents graduating after at least two years at designated A+ high schools, with 95% attendance in grades 9-12, 2.5 unweighted overall GPA, good citizenship, and 50 unpaid tutoring or mentoring hours (up to 25% may be job shadowing). Qualify in Algebra I or an approved higher math end-of-course exam, or through the listed ACT/PreACT math and GPA combinations. Enroll full-time in an eligible degree or certificate program at a participating Missouri community college or vocational/technical institution; approved disability and other enrollment exceptions apply.
notes: Tuition and general fees only, after federal non-loan aid; Pell may eliminate payment. No theology/divinity programs or prior associate/bachelor’s degree. Renewal generally requires 2.5 cumulative GPA, satisfactory progress and completion of 12 fall/spring or 6 summer credits (or 90% of clock hours); initial fall GPA may be 2.0. Eligibility ends at the earliest of 48 months after high school graduation, an associate degree, or 105% of program hours; specified exclusions and military deferrals apply.

provider: Florida Department of Education, Office of Student Financial Assistance
name: Benacquisto Scholarship Program
value: Public institution: in-state cost of attendance minus Bright Futures and National Merit aid. Private institution: highest public-university in-state cost of attendance minus those awards, subject to appropriations.
deadline: No separate Benacquisto application. National Merit Scholar selection and eligible fall enrollment are required; confirm any college-sponsored Merit first-choice deadline. The 2027-28 implementation fact sheet is not published.
apply: Become a National Merit Scholar through a qualifying National Merit award and enroll at an eligible Florida institution. A college-sponsored National Merit award requires that sponsor to be the NMSC first choice and generally continued enrollment there; a national or corporate Merit Scholar award does not require the institution to be a college sponsor.
eligibility: For new recipients, Florida residency, U.S. citizenship or eligible noncitizen status, a qualifying standard Florida diploma or equivalent, and National Merit Scholar status are required. Specified home-education and military/public-service diploma exceptions apply. Enroll in a regionally accredited eligible Florida public or private bachelor’s program in the fall after graduation; an approved deferral of up to one year is possible. New nonresident entrants are not covered by the prior 2018-2022 exception.
notes: National Merit Finalist status alone, a Special Corporate award, or a Presidential award does not qualify. Full-time enrollment is normally at least 12 credits; current statute allows one funded final degree-completion term below 12. Renewal requires a 3.0 cumulative GPA and all enrolled credits earned. Maximum 100% of required program credits, up to five years/ten semesters; approved extended-hours and emergency exceptions apply. The nine 2026-27 college sponsors are not the entire eligible-institution list. Summer funding depends on appropriations; the 2026-27 sheet says it is unavailable.

provider: Florida Department of Education, Office of Student Financial Assistance
name: Florida Bright Futures: Gold Seal Vocational Scholars (GSV)
value: Fixed per-credit or clock-hour award. In 2026-27, career certificates/ATDs receive $39 per semester credit or $1.30 per clock hour; AS/AAS/CCC programs receive $48 or $1.60. The 2027-28 rates are not published.
deadline: For 2027 high school graduates, submit the FFAA October 1, 2026-August 31, 2027. Qualifying tests may be completed through August 31, 2027; midyear graduates have a January 31 test deadline. No deadline time zone stated.
apply: Submit the Florida Financial Aid Application during senior year and track award status. Arrange official school transcript, qualifying test scores and school-certified volunteer/work documentation. Send ACT/SAT scores to a Florida public college/state university or use the stated OSFA reporting option; PERT scores appear on the official transcript.
eligibility: Florida residents who are U.S. citizens or eligible noncitizens and meet Florida diploma/equivalency rules. Required 3.0 weighted GPA in non-elective high school courses, 3.5 unweighted GPA in three full CTE credits, and all subtest minima in one exam type: ACT Reading 19/English 17/Math 19; SAT EBRW 490/Math 480; or PERT Reading 106/Writing 103/Math 114. Complete 30 volunteer hours, 100 paid work hours or a 100-hour combination; students entering grade 9 in 2024-25 or later need 75 volunteer hours for that route. Enroll at least six non-remedial credits in an eligible Florida career/technical program, with specified final-program exceptions.
notes: GSV funds ATD, AS/AAS, CCC and career certificates; it does not fund AA or bachelor’s programs. Maximum 100% of program hours, up to 72 semester hours (60 for ATDs), within five years after graduation. Renewal is automatically evaluated and requires 2.75 unrounded/unweighted cumulative GPA plus earned credits based on funded enrollment (12/9/6 per full/three-quarter/half-time term). Withdrawn-course reimbursement and limited first-year GPA restoration/emergency exceptions apply. Gold Seal CAPE is a separate award.

provider: New York State Higher Education Services Corporation (HESC)
name: NYS STEM Incentive Program
value: Actual tuition or SUNY state-operated undergraduate resident tuition, whichever is less, after other tuition-specific aid. Fees, housing and books are excluded. One undergraduate degree, including an associate/bachelor’s sequence; approved five-year programs may receive five years.
deadline: The current HESC page says applications are closed. No confirmed 2027 application window; the FAQ’s usual October 1-August 15 window is not a dated 2027 announcement.
apply: When open, submit the HESC online application, high school transcript and school-official top-10% verification; applicants must apply as seniors for fall immediately after graduation, subject to approved deferral. Standard route requires FAFSA and NYS Student Aid Payment Application annually. DREAM Act applicants first establish eligibility through that route. Approved recipients sign the service contract.
eligibility: NYS high school graduates in the top 10.0% of their graduating class, entering an approved STEM program full-time at SUNY/CUNY immediately after graduation. Standard route: U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen and 12 continuous months of NY residence. HESC also directs nonresidents and undocumented students to NYS DREAM Act eligibility. No income limit. Complete at least 12 degree-applicable credits each term and maintain 2.5 cumulative GPA from the second semester; approved interruptions may apply.
notes: Program is currently closed. Tuition-only aid; no concurrent full-tuition state scholarship. After completing the degree, reside in NY and work at least 35 hours weekly in an approved STEM occupation for five continuous years, normally beginning within six months. Failure to complete the degree, qualifying service or required reporting converts all payments to a ten-year loan with interest accruing from disbursement; approved hardship/deferment provisions apply. College renewal GPA is not a high school GPA threshold.
